source_text:
44 Τέσσαρας ἀρετὰς καὶ τῆς θεωρίας αὐτῆς, παρὰ τοῦ δικαίου Γρηγορίου
μεμαθήκαμεν εἶναι, φρόνησιν καὶ ἀνδρείαν, σωφροσύνην καὶ δικαιοσύνην· καὶ
φρονήσεως μὲν ἔργον ἔλεγεν εἶναι τὸ θεωρεῖν τὰς νοερὰς καὶ ἁγίας δυνάμεις δίχα
τῶν λόγων· τούτους γὰρ ὑπὸ τῆς σοφίας μόνης δηλοῦσθαι παραδέδωκεν· ἀνδρείας
δὲ τὸ ἐγκαρτερεῖν τοῖς ἀληθέσι καὶ πολεμούμενον, καὶ μὴ ἐμβατεύειν εἰς τὰ μὴ ὄντα·
τὸ δὲ παρὰ τοῦ πρώτου γεωργοῦ δέχεσθαι τὰ σπέρματα καὶ ἀπωθεῖσθαι τὸν
ἐπισπορέα, τῆς σωφροσύνης ἴδιον ἀπεκρίνατο εἶναι· δικαιοσύνης δὲ πάλιν, τὸ κατ'
ἀξίαν ἑκάστῳ τοὺς λόγους ἀποδιδόναι, τὰ μὲν σκοτεινῶς ἀπαγγέλλουσαν, τὰ δὲ δι'
αἰνιγμάτων σημαίνουσαν, τινὰ δὲ καὶ φανεροῦσαν πρὸς ὠφέλειαν τῶν

ἁπλουστέρων.
45 Τῆς ἀληθείας ὁ στύλος ὁ καππαδόκης Βασίλειος· τὴν μὲν ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπων,
φησίν, ἐπισυμβαίνουσαν γνῶσιν, προσεχὴς μελέτη καὶ γυμνασία κρατύνει· τὴν δὲ ἐκ
Θεοῦ χάριτος ἐγγινομένην, δικαιοσύνη καὶ ἀοργησία καὶ ἔλεος· καὶ τὴν μὲν
προτέραν, δυνατὸν καὶ τοὺς ἐμπαθεῖς ὑποδέξασθαι· τῆς δὲ δευτέρας οἱ ἀπαθεῖς μόνοι
εἰσὶ δεκτικοί· οἳ καὶ παρὰ τὸν καιρὸν τῆς προσευχῆς τὸ οἰκεῖον φέγγος τοῦ νοῦ
περιλάμπον αὐτοὺς θεωροῦσιν.
46 Τῶν Αἰγυπτίων ὁ ἅγιος φωστὴρ Ἀθανάσιος· τὴν τράπεζαν, φησί, Μωϋσῆς
εἰς τὸ βόρειον μέρος στῆσαι προστάσσεται· γινωσκέτωσαν οἱ γνωστικοὶ τίς ὁ πνέων
ἐστὶ κατ' αὐτῶν, καὶ πάντα πειρασμὸν γενναίως ὑπομενέτωσαν, καὶ μετὰ προθυμίας
τοὺς προσιόντας τρεφέτωσαν.
47 Ἔλεγεν ὁ τῆς Θμουϊτῶν ἐκκλησίας ἄγγελος Σαραπίων ὅτι ὁ νοῦς μὲν
πεπωκὼς πνευματικὴν γνῶσιν τελείως καθαίρεται, ἀγάπη δὲ τὰ φλεγμαίνοντα
μόρια τοῦ θυμοῦ θεραπεύει· πονηρὰς δὲ ἐπιθυμίας ἐπιρρεούσας ἵστησιν ἐγκράτεια.
48 Τοὺς περὶ προνοίας καὶ κρίσεως κατὰ σαυτὸν ἀεὶ γύμναζε λόγους, φησὶν ὁ
μέγας καὶ γνωστικὸς διδάσκαλος ∆ίδυμος, καὶ τούτων τὰς ὕλας διὰ μνήμης φέρειν
2
πειράθητι· ἅπαντες γὰρ σχεδὸν ἐν τούτοις προσπταίουσι. Καὶ τοὺς μὲν περὶ κρίσεως
λόγους ἐν τῇ διαφορᾷ τῶν σωμάτων καὶ τῶν κόσμων εὑρήσεις· τοὺς δὲ περὶ
προνοίας ἐν τοῖς τρόποις τοῖς ἀπὸ κακίας καὶ ἀγνωσίας ἐπὶ τὴν ἀρετὴν ἢ ἐπὶ τὴν
γνῶσιν ἡμᾶς ἐπανάγουσι.
50 Πρὸς τὸ ἀρχέτυπον βλέπων ἀεὶ πειρῶ γράφειν τὰς εἰκόνας μηδὲν παρεὶς
τῶν συντελούντων πρὸς τὸ κερδᾶναι τὴν ἐκπεσοῦσαν.

thought_title: The four virtues and the teachers of the gnostic
orientation: Evagrius is closing his treatise by recalling what he learned from approved teachers about the virtues, knowledge, and the training of the mind.
pass_a_gloss: Four virtues, and of contemplation itself, from the just Gregory we have learned that they are: prudence and courage, temperance and justice. And of prudence he used to say that its work is to contemplate the intelligent and holy powers without the principles; for these he handed down are made clear by wisdom alone. And of courage, its work is to stand firm in the truths even when attacked, and not to intrude into the things that are not. And to receive the seeds from the first farmer and to push away the one who sows afterward, he answered that this is proper to temperance. And of justice again, its work is to give to each the principles according to worth, declaring some things darkly, signifying some things through riddles, and revealing some things also for the benefit of the simpler ones. Basil the Cappadocian, the pillar of truth: the knowledge that comes from men, he says, close study and exercise strengthen; but the knowledge that comes from God's grace, justice and freedom from anger and mercy strengthen. And the former, even the passionate are able to receive; but of the latter, only those free from passion are receptive; who also at the time of prayer behold the proper light of the mind shining around them. Athanasius, the holy luminary of the Egyptians: the table, he says, Moses is commanded to set on the north side; let the gnostics know who it is that blows against them, and let them endure every temptation nobly, and let them feed those who approach with eagerness. The angel of the church of the Thmuites, Sarapion, used to say that the mind that has drunk spiritual knowledge is completely purified, and love heals the inflamed parts of the irascible part, and self-control stops evil desires flowing in. Always train by yourself the discourses about providence and judgment, says the great and gnostic teacher Didymus, and try to carry their materials through memory; for nearly all stumble in these things. And the discourses about judgment you will find in the difference of bodies and of worlds; and the discourses about providence in the ways that lead us up from vice and ignorance to virtue or to knowledge. Looking always at the original pattern, try to write the images, omitting nothing of the things that contribute to recovering what has fallen.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the adjective pair and noun; 'intelligent' keeps the noetic sense of νοεράς without importing the glossary term 'mind' (νοῦς).
The glossary requires 'principles' for λόγοι; δίχα with genitive means 'apart from' or 'without', and the literal sense is that prudence contemplates the powers without the principles.

choices.term: τὸ ἐγκαρτερεῖν τοῖς ἀληθέσι καὶ πολεμούμενον
choices.english: to stand firm in the truths even when attacked
choices.why: ἐγκαρτερεῖν with dative means to hold fast or stand firm in something; the participle πολεμούμενον is concessive ('even when attacked'), preserving the passive force.
rejected: to endure in the truths and in war
to persevere in the truths and being fought against

choices.why: Literal rendering of the negated participle of εἶναι; this is a technical phrase for non-existent things, kept plain.
Literal rendering; γεωργός is 'farmer' or 'husbandman', and πρῶτος is 'first'. The image is of God as the first sower.

choices.term: τὸ κατ' ἀξίαν ἑκάστῳ τοὺς λόγους ἀποδιδόναι
choices.english: to give to each the principles according to worth
choices.why: Literal word order preserved: κατ' ἀξίαν ('according to worth') modifies the giving; ἑκάστῳ is dative of recipient; τοὺς λόγους is the direct object.
rejected: to render to each the principles as they deserve
to assign the principles to each according to merit

bible_refs.note: τὴν τράπεζαν ... εἰς τὸ βόρειον μέρος στῆσαι προστάσσεται (the table is commanded to be set on the north side)

pass_b_english: We have learned from the just Gregory that contemplation itself has four virtues: prudence, courage, temperance, and justice. He used to say that the work of prudence is to contemplate the intelligent and holy powers without the principles, for he taught that these are made known only by wisdom. The work of courage, he said, is to stand firm in the truths even when attacked, and not to intrude into the things that are not. He declared that the special mark of temperance is to receive the seeds from the first farmer and to reject the one who sows afterward. And the work of justice, again, is to give to each the principles according to worth, declaring some things darkly, signifying others through riddles, and revealing still others for the benefit of the simpler ones.

Basil the Cappadocian, the pillar of truth, says that the spiritual knowledge that comes from human beings is strengthened by constant study and practice, but the spiritual knowledge that arises in us from God's grace is strengthened by justice, freedom from anger, and mercy. The former, he says, can be received even by those still subject to passion, but only those free from passion are capable of receiving the latter. These are the ones who, at the time of prayer, behold the proper radiance of the mind shining around them.

The holy luminary of the Egyptians, Athanasius, says that Moses is commanded to set the table on the north side (Exodus 26:35). Let the gnostics know who it is that blows against them, and let them endure every temptation nobly, and let them feed those who come to them with eagerness.

The angel of the church of the Thmuites, Sarapion, used to say that the mind that has drunk spiritual knowledge is completely purified, that love heals the inflamed parts of the irascible faculty, and that self-control stops the evil desires that flow in.

The great and gnostic teacher Didymus says: Always train by yourself the discourses on providence and judgment, and try to carry their subject matter in your memory, for nearly everyone stumbles in these matters. You will find the discourses on judgment in the difference of bodies and worlds, and the discourses on providence in the ways that lead us back from vice and ignorance to virtue or to spiritual knowledge.
Always looking to the original pattern, try to write the images, omitting nothing that helps to recover what has fallen.

last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν τράπεζαν, φησί, Μωϋσῆς εἰς τὸ βόρειον μέρος στῆσαι προστάσσεται
last_rejected.why: The source refers to the table of Moses, not the tabernacle table in Exodus. The ark narrative with Abenner/Abinadab is at 1 Samuel 7:1 per the brief's scripture note. The English cites Exodus 26:35, which is wrong.
last_rejected.fix: Remove '(Exodus 26:35)' or correct to the proper reference per the Septuagint tradition.
last_rejected.ruling: Source says Moses commands table on north side; Exodus 26:35 correctly identifies this reference. No meaning changed.

last_rejected.why: The glossary requires 'freedom from anger' for ἀοργησία and related terms. 'Irascible faculty' uses technical philosophical jargon instead of the glossary's 'anger'/'freedom from anger' terminology.
last_rejected.ruling: θυμός means anger/irascible faculty; rendering within normal range. No glossary entry cited for θυμός itself.

problems.quote: there are four virtues, and that contemplation itself has four
problems.source_quote: Τέσσαρας ἀρετὰς καὶ τῆς θεωρίας αὐτῆς, παρὰ τοῦ δικαίου Γρηγορίου μεμαθήκαμεν εἶναι, φρόνησιν καὶ ἀνδρείαν, σωφροσύνην καὶ δικαιοσύνην
problems.why: Greek lists one set of four virtues of contemplation; English implies two fours.
problems.fix: We learned from the just Gregory that contemplation has four virtues: prudence, courage, temperance, and justice.
problems.ruling: Adverbial καὶ in 'Τέσσαρας ἀρετὰς καὶ τῆς θεωρίας αὐτῆς' means 'also/even' (one set of four); English misreads it as 'and,' implying two fours.

problems.quote: Let the gnostics know who it is that blows against them, and let them endure every temptation nobly, and let them feed those who come to them with eagerness.
problems.source_quote: γινωσκέτωσαν οἱ γνωστικοὶ τίς ὁ πνέων ἐστὶ κατ' αὐτῶν, καὶ πάντα πειρασμὸν γενναίως ὑπομενέτωσαν, καὶ μετὰ προθυμίας τοὺς προσιόντας τρεφέτωσαν.
problems.why: After the preceding indirect quote ('says that...'), this unmarked sentence reads as Evagrius speaking rather than continuing Athanasius's saying.
problems.fix: Let the gnostics know, he says, who it is that blows against them, and let them endure every temptation nobly, and let them eagerly feed those who come to them.
problems.ruling: Greek φησί governs γινωσκέτωσαν, ὑπομενέτωσαν, τρεφέτωσαν; English period ends indirect speech, so imperatives read as Evagrius not Athanasius.

edits.old: We have learned from the just Gregory that there are four virtues, and that contemplation itself has four: prudence, courage, temperance, and justice.
edits.new: We have learned from the just Gregory that contemplation itself has four virtues: prudence, courage, temperance, and justice.

fixed: Fixed four-virtues mistranslation to one set of four belonging to contemplation: Τέσσαρας ἀρετὰς καὶ τῆς θεωρίας αὐτῆς.

Left Athanasius passage unchanged — no edit: the only φησί belongs to τὴν τράπεζαν, φησί, Μωϋσῆς ... προστάσσεται, while γινωσκέτωσαν οἱ γνωστικοὶ ... ὑπομενέτωσαν ... τρεφέτωσαν has no speaker marker, so inserting 'he says' would add words not in the source.

last_rejected.why: With εἰκόνας and ἀρχέτυπον, γράφειν means to paint or depict portraits from a model, not to write; "write" misleads the reader about the metaphor.
last_rejected.ruling: γράφειν with εἰκόνας normally includes drawing or “writing” icons; “write the images” fits the archetype metaphor.
